TORI & TJ

The Funny
Greyhound

The sun came up. The sky was blue.
Tori tied her sneaker shoe.
TJ hopped from stair to stair.
“School today! Let’s hurry there!”

1

They walked to school past Oak and Main,
past the puddle, past the drain,
past the flag, and then they found
something funny hanging around.

2

There on the wall in gray and blue,
a painted dog — and then he GREW.
He blinked. He stretched. And with a POP,
he leaped right off his painted spot!

3

He left a hole shaped just like him,
with pointy ears and legs so slim.
TJ plopped down on the ground —
“A REAL LIVE DOG! A FUNNY HOUND!”

4

Tori grinned and looked around.
“Why are you so funny, Greyhound?”
“Because,” he said, “I chase my tail!
I almost catch it. Then I fail.”
He spun around. He spun some more.
He bonked the pole and hit the floor.

5

He zipped inside and down the hall.
The floor was shiny. Greyhounds fall!
He slid past doors — one, two, three, four —
and crashed right through the closet door.
The mops fell down. The brooms did too.
He wore a bucket like a shoe.

6

In Tori’s class he found a seat.
The chair was small. He looked so sweet —
then CREAK! and CRACK! and down he went,
his legs up high, his tail all bent.
The teacher sighed. The class all cheered.
“This school just got a little weird!”

7

At lunchtime he picked up a tray.
Then two. Then ten. “I’ve got it! Hey—”
The jello wobbled. Whoa! Look out!
SPLAT went the noodles on his snout!

8

The slide was small. The dog was tall.
He scrunched up like a fuzzy ball.
He zipped! He zoomed! He flew! And then —
he landed in the sand. “AGAIN!”

9

“You have to whisper,” Tori said.
He nodded his big doggy head.
He whispered “SHHHH!” — a BIT too loud.
(A shout like that is not allowed!)
Then books rained down — bonk! bonk! — kerplop!
He wore them like a hat on top.

10

In gym he grabbed the long jump rope.
He jumped. He tripped. He spun. He — NOPE.
The rope wound round him, head to toe.
So Tori tied it in a bow!

11

Then Tori asked him one more round:
“Why are you SO funny, Greyhound?”
He knelt down low. He said, “You see,
a school can feel too big to me.
But nobody feels scared right now,
when someone silly takes a bow.”

12

The bell rang out. The day was done.
The Greyhound waved to everyone.
He climbed back in his cozy wall
and smiled his best goodnight to all.

13

So every day at half past eight,
Tori waves. She’s never late.
TJ giggles, round and round —
“GOOD MORNING, FUNNY GREYHOUND!”

14
THE END
